articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Speedrunners Have Already Found New Ways to Break the Remake
articles.summary: From quicker movement to sending Link to space, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time speedrunners have already found a few ways to break the remake.
body: One of the best things about a new Zelda game is seeing just how quickly players can speed through it, but Nintendo's latest video game being a remake presents a unique situation. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has accumulated some of the most bizarre speedrunning strategies in its 28 years on the market, and in just a few days, the Nintendo Switch 2 remake looks like it will live up to that legacy.

Creative players started peeling back the layers of the new version of Link and Zelda's classic adventure just hours after it launched November 5. Even just moments into its life, they've discovered some seemingly useful (and hilarious) ways to break the game, with more almost certainly to be discovered in the weeks, months, and years ahead. Let's start with what might be the most common tactic under investigation so far: sending Link hurdling into the air at high speed.
points: From quicker movement to sending Link to space, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time speedrunners have already found a few ways to break the remake.

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Opening Weekend Box Office Breaks A Foreign-Language Film Records
articles.summary: Godzilla Minus Zero had a strong opening weekend, grossing more at the domestic box office than any live action foreign-language film before it. On top of that, a higher percentage of people sought out premium screens, like IMAX, to watch it even more than they did for The Odyssey earlier this year.
body: Deadline's reporting highlights that Godzilla Minus Zero is estimated to have grossed $32 million. Although American-made Godzilla movies have made more during their first weekend in theaters, this is a very impressive feat for a foreign-language film, as they rarely do this well at the domestic box office unless they're connected to an anime. As mentioned, this opening is record-breaking for a live-action one.

Godzilla Minus Zero's performance also shows the value of making movies that people want to see on the biggest screen possible, as around 74% of its gross came from IMAX or other premium large format screens. In comparison, The Odyssey got a lot of attention because around 54% of its opening weekend gross came from PLF screens. 2026 has certainly shown that there's demand for blockbusters that embrace that opulent style of filmmaking beyond a typical superhero movie.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Thankfully Resists FromSoftware’s Influence
articles.summary: This year in video games, I’ve swung a digital sword more times than I can count. Thrilling action games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Phantom Blade Zero have gotten the feel of a sword fight down to a science, as steel clashes and sparks fly in spectacular fashion.
body: The Switch 2 remake builds on the combat of Link’s 1998 adventure in careful but effective fashion. The Master Sword feels more powerful than ever thanks to killer sound design and a bit of visual pizazz on impact. What the remake doesn’t do, however, is change Link’s moves to give him the most widely used trick in modern action games: the parry. There’s no deflection to be found in Ocarina of Time ’s remake, and that makes a seemingly simple combat system stand out in an unexpectedly refreshing way.

Compared to many modern games, Ocarina of Time ’s swordplay doesn’t require much mastery from players. Aside from a charged spin attack and a leaping slash, Link’s offensive options are limited. Lock on, swing the sword, hit the enemy, and that’s basically all you need to know. Sure, you can block attacks with your shield or use one of your items to switch it up, but you’re always going to follow the same motions to take out a Deku Baba with consistent strikes.

articles.title: Phasmophobia players raise over $230,000 for heart charity, more than double last year's total
articles.summary: The Phasmophobia community has raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.
body: Developer Kinetic Games announced the final figure for this year's Ghost Hunts for Hearts event on 6th November. The charity drive ran from 26th October to 2nd November, and more than 500 streamers signed up to take part. That's the biggest turnout yet for a creator fundraiser run by Heart Liive, the American Heart Association's streaming initiative.

Streamers who fundraised could hand out an event-exclusive Advocate ID Card and Badge to their viewers as a Twitch Drop. Kinetic set a target of $200,000 at the start of the week, and once players sailed past it, an animated version of the card and badge set unlocked for all.

"The Phasmophobia community never fails to amaze us, and this year they've outdone themselves," said Tom Dent, lead social media and player experience manager at Kinetic Games. "Thank you to every streamer, viewer and player who took part."
Phasmophobia launched in Early Access in September 2020, and sends teams of up to four players into haunted locations to gather evidence of what's lurking there.

articles.title: Speedrunners Already Breaking The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Remake
articles.summary: Speedrunners have had their hands on the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for a couple of days now, and some funky tricks have already been discovered.
body: Videos from YouTubers like Kethaldo and Knightpohtayto, as well as Bluesky user Mircacle, show how actor jumping is essentially a glitched super jump that players can do with certain aimable tools in Ocarina of Time. To perform the trick, players have to find a movable object, or "actor," in the game's environments, like a chest or movable tombstone. When standing on it, players then have to shoot, press the lock-on button (ZL by default) before it's done being used, and then jump as soon as the animation ends.

By doing this, Link can jump much higher than he is supposed to. When used at certain parts of Ocarina of Time's levels, it's possible to jump even higher and skip massive swaths of the game. Right now, it's easiest to pull off when using the hookshot, so actor jumps are worth attempting once you get it.

Nintendo has yet to patch this trick out of the remake, so the speedrunning community is avidly taking advantage of it less than a week after the game's launch. Compared to some other speedrunning tricks in the remake, action jumps are very easy to perform, too.

articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Guaranteed a GOTY Nomination. It Will Never Win
articles.summary: Here are the four remakes that were nominated: Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 4, Final Fantasy 7 Remake, and Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth. Apart from the obvious, what these four games have in common is their bold retellings of the original stories in a completely modern gaming vernacular, sometimes…
body: Here are just a few of the dozens of video game remakes released since The Game Awards began in 2014 that were not nominated for Game of the Year: Shadow of the Colossus. The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening. Demon's Souls. The Last of Us Part 1. Silent Hill 2. All acclaimed new versions of canonical classics, and all among the best-reviewed games of their respective years.

Nintendo's new version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time sits somewhere in between these two groups. It is, for the most part, reverently faithful to the original story and design, with a few smart modernizations. But it does make bold artistic choices in perhaps the most dramatic visual overhaul of any remake yet.

Ocarina of Time is not quite "what this game would be like if you made it today," which is the approach taken by Capcom and Square Enix on Resident Evil and Final Fantasy 7. It's more classical in its design than that. But nor is it a painstaking recreation of a masterwork like, say, Bluepoint's exquisite PlayStation 4 version of Shadow of the Colossus. It's willing to look and feel different from the source material.

articles.summary: Anyone hoping to buy Mass Effect from EA and finish what BioWare started needs to get saving now, as it could cost over $200 million (£150m).
body: That's according to BioWare co-founder Trent Oster, who reckons that's what a new Mass Effect game would need to meet fans' expectations.
"The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of 'AAA' development," Oster said on Twitter/X, as spotted by GamesRadar.

articles.title: Missing teenager rescued after reaching out to another player in Among Us
articles.summary: A teenager who went missing in Utah more than 17 months ago has been rescued from a home in Oregon after she got in touch with another young player in Among Us.
body: According to a federal criminal complaint reported by Newsweek and KUTV (via IGN ), the girl, who was 15 when she disappeared from Garden City, Utah, on 29th May 2025, began chatting with another teenager in Among Us on or around 15th October this year.

The pair later moved their conversation to a different social media app, where she told them who she was and that she was being held against her will in Oregon. She had been given a phone with no cellular data, which meant she could only get online via wi-fi.

The other teen told their parent, who contacted the FBI on 1st November. Agents listened in on a video call between the parent and the girl, and she was recovered from the house later that day. She is now 17.
Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was arrested during a traffic stop.

articles.title: Epic Reveals Drop Rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token Following Pressure From Fans
articles.summary: Epic Games has revealed the drop rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token after backlash surrounding the infamous in-game pickup saw fans try to report the studio to the FTC.
body: It's been just one week since Epic turned the Item Shop on its head with the launch of its Treasure Hunters mini-season November 1. At the center of the backlash is the Pirate Token, an ultra-rare drop that grants access to the Pirate Shop and effectively makes just about every item in the shop free for 14 days.

It's an in-game collectible with unprecedented value, so naturally, it's sent players into a frenzy as they turn over every chest in hopes of finding one for themselves. The problem with a token like this, players have argued, is that they should probably be made aware of the odds of actually finding it so they don't gamble their time on chests that could very likely never yield results. It's transparency that Epic has failed to provide – until now.
points: Epic Games has revealed the drop rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token after backlash surrounding the infamous in-game pickup saw fans try to report the studio to the FTC.

articles.title: Dominic Armato, voice of Guybrush Threepwood, has always loved LucasArts' adventure games, but there's one he still can't get into: 'I get 10 minutes in and I'm like, oh, this is tedious, man'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Dominic Armato is adventure game royalty, but an early adventure game experience almost killed his enthusiasm for videogames: "The one that really sticks in my head is The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy," he says. "It was just evil. I was a kid, and I'm trying to play this game that's one of the most difficult text adventure games ever written … It's not a happy memory. It's a miracle that I stuck with videogames at all."

Yet persist with games Armato did, becoming an avid fan of the point 'n' click adventures designed by LucasArts. This led Armato to audition for and be cast as mighty pirate Guybrush Threepwood for 1997's The Curse of Monkey Island. It's a role he would reprise for every subsequent Monkey Island game, including the remakes of The Secret of Monkey Island and Monkey Island 2, as well as 2022's excellent Return to Monkey Island.
points: He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.

articles.title: Inspired by Dark Messiah and Thief, this stealth game sees you sneak through a medieval megastructure prowled by undead guards
articles.summary: It's a great time to be a fan of both Thief: The Dark Project and Dark Messiah of Might and Magic. A Thief remaster from Nightdive—which features a new campaign—is coming next month, while Dark Messiah is getting a Ubisoft-approved community edition that adds co-op, new modes and more.
body: Until earlier today, I hadn't seen a game inspired by both Thief and Dark Messiah at the same time (apart from Dishonored, I suppose, though that was made by Dark Messiah developers Arkane, so I'm not sure that counts). But that all changed when The Citadel Project snuck through my eyes and booted my ignorance right out of my brain.

Created by solo outfit Reliquary Software, The Citadel Project synthesises the designs of Thief and Dark Messiah with first-person indie gaming's current fascination with megastructures. It casts you as a sickle-wielding prisoner trying to escape a sprawling medieval fortress prowled by shambling undead guards.

The Citadel Project's Thief leanings are most obvious at a glance. Environments are shrouded in shadow, stealth is your greatest asset, and your character carries a crossbow that can fire various kinds of bolts—including water bolts and moss quarrels. The Dark Messiah DNA, meanwhile, is most prominent in the physics engine. Alongside being able to slip past enemies, your character can give them a hard shove in the back, shunting them off ledges and into conveniently placed spike traps.

articles.title: WoW: Forever is the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history, says Blizzard
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is the biggest launch in the MMO's history, pulling in more concurrent players than any previous WoW launch.
body: Blizzard shared the news on social media yesterday (7th November), saying the new edition, which launched on 4th November, broke records for both peak concurrent players and returning players.
"Congratulations everyone, you made history!" the official World of Warcraft account posted. "This is all because of you, the players. From all of us, thank you!"

The game hasn't just tempted back lapsed players. In a follow-up post, executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale said it brought in the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years.
"Welcome all! We're so happy you're here experiencing Azeroth for the first time alongside those of us playing it for the first time... again," she wrote.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever is the biggest launch in the MMO's history, pulling in more concurrent players than any previous WoW launch.

articles.title: This massive mod essentially turns Skyrim into a persistent MMO 'where player actions create lasting consequences'
articles.summary: PC gaming isn't short of multiplayer fantasy adventures these days, but there is still something alluring about the idea of playing Skyrim with pals. Some mods have facilitated small-scale Skyrim multiplayer in the past, like the cooperative mod Skyrim Together.
body: According to its ModDB page, Aurbis transforms Skyrim's solo adventure into "a persistent world where player actions create lasting consequences", snythesising Skyrim's existing experience with a bunch of multiplayer and MMO-like systems. It's designed with roleplaying in mind, though the mod's creators stress that RP is not mandatory, and players can focus on other elements like cooperative dungeon runs or PvP play if they so choose.

The list of changes and additions to Aurbis is impressive, running from character creation outward. The retooled character builder is designed to let avatars "develop over time instead of becoming powerful immediately", though it also lets players start with vampirism or lycanthropy for roleplaying purposes.

Those roles are heavily defined by the player's choice of Birthsign, which affects how efficiently skills develop. Crafting professions are supported by a player-driven economy that factors in bank accounts, property ownership and player-created quests, while activities like combat are designed to be dangerous and reward "preparation, equipment, specialisation and teamwork."
points: PC gaming isn't short of multiplayer fantasy adventures these days, but there is still something alluring about the idea of playing Skyrim with pals.

articles.title: As Wardogs Season 3 looms, Bulkhead claims to have built 'one of the world's most sophisticated anti-cheat systems', assisted by 'machine learning and AI'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Wardogs enjoyed an incredible launch, but Season 2 was very much Bulkhead's 'difficult second album' phase of live service development. A cash-incentive experiment to rebalance the game's weaker blue team was dropped just one day it went live, while the studio's broader attempt to address player concerns ended up sucking a lot of the fun out of the military FPS.

Now, with Season 3 on the horizon, Bulkhead has addressed the mistakes the studio made with Season 2 and discussed how the new season will address them. It's a tale that involves a new map, new modes, new upgrade paths, and an AI-powered anticheat.

The Road to Season 3 video kicks off with a mea culpa from Bulkhead. "Whilst learning to adapt to running a live service, we decided with good intent to try to respond to negative reviews with actions rather than words," Howard Philpott, Bulkhead's UI/UX director, says in the video. "When the patch notes dropped, on paper the reaction was great. But in reality, when the season went live, the sentiment went quickly downhill.

articles.title: The Sunday Papers
articles.summary: Sundays are for waking up covered in sand. The roof of your house is missing. A small man stands in the emptied bed of a dump truck. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," he says. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," he repeats.
body: Is he about to sit on your face? WAIT, THAT'S NOW ILLEGAL HERE IN THE UK. NO, PLEASE, DON'T SIT ON MY-time seems to slow as the bare backside approaches your visage. As its cheeks prepare to become as sandy as yours, you hear its wielder say: "And we thought, hey, given the moment..."

Panicking, you scrabble for anything to say which might free you before something that might get a British MP's hackles up can occur. "Things first went awry when I turned up for my appointment to find a tall German man wearing a cowboy hat asking a PR if he could play the game," you blurt out. The posterior momentarily stops moving towards you. Buoyed, you continue to tell a story you heard from VGC 's Chris Scullion.
I was asked if I minded sharing my one-to-one appointment with this chap too, to which my inherent British cowardly courtesy kicked in and I lied that it was perfectly fine.

"I want drums", he said as he entered the room. "We are playing Dani California by Red Hot Chili Peppers." Rather than ask him whether he also fancied telling me where I was going for dinner later, I picked up my guitar and went along with it, eager to just play the game.
